Name: Twisha Asher
Bio: Twisha Asher is a fifth-year student in economics at the CUNY Graduate Center. She is working on a dissertation about factors that influence wealth inequality and intergenerational wealth mobility.

Name: Frincasco Di Biase
Bio: Frincasco Di Biase studied economics at the University of Chile and spent his primary and secondary school years in a French school. Since 2019, he has lived in Rome. Di Biase is very interested in social economics and is passionate about cinema.

Name: Franziska Disslbacher
Bio: Franziska Disslbacher studies wealth and income inequality, intergenerational mobility, and the measurement of inequalities. She is especially interested in the mechanisms and institutions that link inequalities in outcomes and opportunities and is affiliated with the Research Institute Economics of Inequality in Vienna. Previously she held research positions at the departments of economics and socioeconomics at WU Vienna and was a visiting researcher at the University of California, Berkeley, and the Luxembourg Institute of Socio-Economic Research. She has a PhD in economics and social sciences from WU Vienna.

Name: Ignacio Flores
Position: CUNY Graduate Center & Roma Tre University & PSE**Data Architect**(2021 - present)
Bio: Ignacio Flores is an economist whose research investigates socioeconomic inequality, including its measurement, its origins, and its consequences, with a general perspective. He is the coordinator for Latin America and the Caribbean at the World Inequality Database at the Paris School of Economics. Previously he was a postdoctoral researcher at INSEADÕs James M. and Cathleen D. Stone Centre for the Study of Wealth Inequality. Flores earned his Ph.D. in economics from Paris 1 PanthŽon-Sorbonne University.

Name: Demetrio Guzzardi
Position: Sant'Anna School of Advanced Studies **Research Assistant**(2022 - present)
Fullposition: Sant'Anna School of Advanced Studies **Research Assistant**(2022 - present)
Bio: Demetrio Guzzardi is a third-year PhD student in economics at the SantÕAnna School of Advanced Studies in Pisa, Italy. He holds an MSc in economics jointly from the Paris School of Economics, Sorbonne Paris-1, the Universidad Aut—noma de Barcelona, and CaÕFoscari University. His research interests include income distribution, wealth distribution, fiscal policies, and generational and intergenerational mobility. His current research projects focus on the estimation of income distribution and related fiscal policies in Italy and on the estimation of inheritance flows in various countries.

Name: Adam Rego Johnson
Bio: Adam Rego Johnson is a master's student in political science, with a focus on public policy, at the CUNY Graduate Center. He previously studied sociology and political science at the New College of Florida, where he conducted a case study for his honors thesis on urban planning design charrettes and their use as a deliberative democratic institution.

Name: Arthur B. Kennickell
Position: The Stone Center, CUNY Graduate Center**Affiliated Scholar**(2017 - present)
Fullposition: The Stone Center, CUNY Graduate Center**Affiliated Scholar**(2017 - present)

Name: Mei Li
Bio: Mei Li is a PhD candidate in economics at the CUNY Graduate Center, and an adjunct faculty member at New York University. She formerly worked as an economist at AIG and at other financial institutions.

Name: Salvatore Morelli
Position: Roma Tre University**Director of the Wealth Inequality Project**(2017 - present)
Fullposition: Roma Tre University**Director of the Wealth Inequality Project**(2017 - present)
Bio: Salvatore Morelli is the director of the Wealth Inequality Project and a former research assistant professor at the CUNY Graduate Center. He is currently an assistant professor in public economics in the Law Department at the Roma Tre University. He holds a DPhil in economics from the University of Oxford and is a research associate at the Center for Studies of Economics and Finance**(CSEF) at the University of Naples Federico II.

Name: Qiyao Pan
Bio: Qiyao Pan is a second-year PhD student in sociology at the CUNY Graduate Center. Her research interests include social and spatial demography, urban sociology, and socioeconomic inequality.

Name: Gonçalo Pessa Costa
Bio: GonÃ§alo Pessa Costa is a PhD student at the CUNY Graduate Center, and an adjunct lecturer at Brooklyn College. His areas of research include market power in housing and labor markets, and inequalities. He was an economist-statistician in the central bank of Portugal before joining the Stone Center team. His moral compass and working-class background are inseparable.

Name: Marco Ranaldi
Bio: Marco Renaldi is a lecturer**(assistant professor) of economics at University College London's School of Slavonic and East European Studies and an associated researcher at the GC Wealth Project. Previously he was a postdoctoral scholar at the Stone Center; a consultant at the Development Research Group of the World Bank in Washington, D.C.; and a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford. He holds a PhD from the Paris School of Economics and the University of Paris 1 PanthŽon-Sorbonne.

Name: Giacomo Rella
Position: Roma Tre University &  ESG-UQAM**Postdoctoral Scholar**(2021 - present)
Bio: Giacomo Rella is a postdoctoral researcher in the Law Department at Roma Tre University. Previously he was a trainee at the European Central Bank and a visiting researcher at Ghent University and at the University of Massachusetts Boston. He holds a PhD in economics from the Universities of Siena, Pisa, and Florence. He is a member of the Financial Stability Working Group of the Young Scholar Initiative. His research fields include macroeconomics, monetary policy, wealth inequality, and macroeconomic history.

Name: Ana Laura Rojas Silvero
Bio: Ana Laura Rojas Silvero is a third-year PhD student in economics at the CUNY Graduate Center, a research assistant at the Stone Center, and an adjunct lecturer at CUNY. She holds a master's in public administration and economic law from the University of Salamanca**(Spain) and a MS in economics from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. She was an economist in the central bank of Paraguay before moving to the United States to pursue graduate studies.

Name: Manuel Schechtl
Bio: __Manuel Schechtl is a sociologist who studies the policy determinants of poverty and of income and wealth inequality. His research is centered around different dimensions of tax policy and their consequences. Before joining the Stone Center, he was a research associate at Humboldt-University Berlin, where he earned his PhD in 2022.

Name: Jasmine Simington
Bio: Jasmine Simington is a sociologist who studies how households build wealth, racial wealth disparities, and the effects of environmental disasters on housing assets. Her research on intestate inheritance examines how property law influences wealth inequality. She earned a Ph.D. in public policy and sociology from the University of Michigan and a B.A. in sociology from Yale University, and previously worked at the Urban Institute.
